articles.title: GTA 6 Is Like The Olympics – “A Rare Cultural Moment” With Massive Ripple Effects
articles.summary: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19.
body: Francis Lawrence, the director of the new Hunger Games movie Sunrise on the Reaping, which comes out a day after GTA 6, has said he hopes people can find the time to play the game and watch his movie. In short, GTA 6 is seen by some as a black hole that will suck up time, attention, and money from the broader gaming economy--and even workplaces, as people dive into the 80-hour game they've been waiting a decade to play.

To help make sense of, and contextualize, the enormity of GTA 6's looming launch, GameSpot caught up with Bart Spiegel of the global professional services and research company PricewaterhouseCoopers, or PwC. He told GameSpot that GTA 6 is "something much bigger than a traditional entertainment launch," and is more akin to an event like the Olympics.
He believes GTA 6 is a "rare cultural moment" that "commands extraordinary attention and creates economic activity well beyond the event itself."
points: After years of development, multiple delays, and what can only be assumed to be one of the biggest production budgets ever, Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19.

articles.title: GTA 6 Leak Seemingly Reveals Official Album's Full Track List Days Before Launch
articles.summary: The full track list for Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album seems to have leaked online just days before GTA 6 's launch. Rockstar Games just can't catch a break. After weeks of unprecedented leaks were published online, even more information about GTA 6 has found its way onto the internet, this time…
body: As 13 years turns into just a few days, more leaks felt inevitable. The latest breach arrived in the form of a video shared on social media from what appears to be a Barnes & Noble-like retailer. The main clip being passed around is still up hours later and shows the front, back, and spines of the Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album's double LP vinyl. As you might have guessed, the $50 soundtrack isn't planned to hit store shelves until November 19, 2026.

Although there are likely even more tunes tucked into the game itself, an early glimpse at the GTA 6 soundtrack means we now know every song and artist featured on its official album. Rolling Stone has confirmed the track list with its sources. We won't beat around the bush; you can see the full Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album track list below.

articles.title: League of Legends: New Dawn Unveiled With Debut Trailer, Riot Announces Major Overhaul Coming in 2027
articles.summary: At the 2026 League of Legends World Championship Finals, Riot Games officially unveiled League of Legends: New Dawn. The large-scale update is scheduled for 2027 and will bring changes to the game's client, Summoner's Rift, visuals, and gameplay, marking the beginning of a new chapter for one of…
body: New Dawn introduces what Riot described as an "all-encompassing" update to League, touching almost every aspect of its experience. "This is the start of a new era for League, a new journey," said Paul Bellezza, League's executive producer, in New Dawn's first official trailer. Riot is expected to share the full reveal of New Dawn this coming January.

The announcement came with a trailer shown at Worlds Finals that offered the first glimpse of what League players can expect from New Dawn, and the changes appear to go beyond simple refreshed graphics. The first noticeable change is a redesigned champion selection screen, which looks much closer to the modern interface found in Wild Rift, League's mobile game. The footage also hints at a new or reworked rune system, which seems to have a much bigger impact on the gameplay than ever before.

articles.title: Tomb Raider Remake Gameplay Changes Are Dividing Fans
articles.summary: Amazon Game Studios has released the sixth installment in its behind-the-scenes series about the development of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis. The remake of Lara Croft's original 1996 adventure is set to be released next year and will update the game for modern players.
body: The "Combat & Progression Reimagined" video posted on the official Tomb Raider YouTube channel this summer gives an in-depth look at a handful of new systems coming in Legacy of Atlantis. Game director Raul Siquera details one major addition to the remake: Focus.

"When you're taking damage, dealing damage, dodging attacks, you're building your Focus meter," Siquera explained, "Focus allows you to slow down time around you and showcase some of the things that Lara used to do in 1996." In practice this lets players unlock more of Lara's iconic acrobatic moves after building Focus.

Design director Jason Epps detailed two more changes in Legacy of Atlantis: a skill tree and herb collecting. Both of these elements are heavily inspired by mechanics in Crystal Dynamics' Survivor Trilogy, which revolved more around Lara needing to scavenge for materials and upgrade her skills. "When I played the Survivor series and I could suddenly affect and increase Lara's power in the game, I felt much more engaged," said Epps. Crafting takes on a Resident Evil -style system, letting players make items that heal Lara but also give her buffs.
points: Amazon Game Studios has released the sixth installment in its behind-the-scenes series about the development of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.
The remake of Lara Croft's original 1996 adventure is set to be released next year and will update the game for modern players.

articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem Star Hopes Grace Ashcroft Has 'a Long Way to Go' Even if She Won't 'Ever Be a Leon Character'
articles.summary: Grace Ashcroft actress Angela Sant'Albano doesn't think her Resident Evil Requiem hero will "ever be a Leon character," but she's still hoping "there's a long way to go with her." The person behind one of 2026's standout video game roles laid out her hopes for the future during an interview with…
body: "I would really love to see how her relationship with Leon blossoms," Sant'Albano explained. "I think we have a beautiful mentorship, almost brotherly, sisterly relationship brewing. And I also want to know what happens with her and Emily."

Assuming you chose the 'good' ending, Resident Evil Requiem closes with the series' one-liner expert, Leon S. Kennedy, alive and Grace taking Emily under her wing. It painted a bright future for the crew, and although it almost certainly won't last, it did give the developers at Capcom plenty of room to grow new and old characters alike.

Despite some pretty deep roots in Resident Evil lore, Grace's story in the franchise is really only getting started in Resident Evil Requiem. So far, there's been no word on whether she'll stick around for additional entries and eventually stand toe-to-toe with other protagonists like Ethan Winters or Chris Redfield. Judging by the strong impression she made when her debut game launched in February, we wouldn't be surprised to see her back at some point down the line.

articles.title: Forget Ganon, Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Most Overlooked Boss Finally Gets Its Due
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is iconic for plenty of reasons, but a big part of that is thanks to its villain. Ganondorf is one of gaming’s great bad guys, a reputation that has only been enhanced by appearances in later games like Wind Waker and Tears of the Kingdom.
body: First introduced in Ocarina of Time, Twinrova makes for one of the best bosses in Zelda history. In the Spirit Temple, Link encounters two evil sorceresses who serve Ganondorf, Kotake and Koume. They’re classic witches: a pair of bickering old ladies flying around on brooms. The character concept is fun enough on its own, but the fight itself is memorable, too. Link has to use his Mirror Shield to absorb their elemental attacks (fire and ice) and reflect them back at the witches. It all culminates with the duo coming together Transformers-style to become Twinrova, an even more powerful witch.

The sisters’ real star-turn moment happens after Link vanquishes their Twinrova form and they separate once more. Halos appear above both witches’ heads as they begin floating up towards a light. That sets them off into a panic as they realize they are dying, prompting an unexpectedly great sketch comedy routine.
Koume: Who are you calling senile?! Is that how you treat your older sister?
points: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is iconic for plenty of reasons, but a big part of that is thanks to its villain.
Ganondorf is one of gaming’s great bad guys, a reputation that has only been enhanced by appearances in later games like Wind Waker and Tears of the Kingdom.

articles.title: 9 Giant-Sized Changes Marvel Made to Ant-Man After Edgar Wright Left
articles.summary: As Wright has explained in interviews, he was excited to be on the ground floor of something, setting the tone for what the MCU would become. He wanted to do a superhero movie where it was still emblematic of the director, in keeping with their body of work.
body: In May 2014, it was announced that Edgar Wright, best known for movies like Shaun of the Dead and Scott Pilgrim vs. the World, would no longer be directing Marvel ’s Ant-Man movie. The news was shocking because Wright was not just a director-for-hire like some Marvel filmmakers have been. Wright first began crafting his Ant-Man film with co-writer Joe Cornish in the early 2000s, before the Marvel Cinematic Universe was even a thing. When the MCU began to develop, Wright’s Ant-Man was one of the earliest confirmed projects. Wright was even a part of the MCU’s first panel back in 2006.

Part of the problem was timing. Ant-Man was originally a Phase One MCU movie, with only loose connective tissue to the other films. But Wright asked that Ant-Man be pushed back so that he could direct The World’s End first. This was because his producing partner, Eric Fellner, had been diagnosed with cancer and he wanted to finish their “Cornetto Trilogy” while Fellner still could.

articles.title: 'It Felt Criminal' — Adam Driver Still Can't Believe How Disney Handled Canceled Star Wars Movie The Hunt for Ben Solo
articles.summary: Adam Driver still can't believe Disney killed his Star Wars movie, The Hunt for Ben Solo, and has now gone so far as to say that the move "felt criminal." The Kylo Ren/Ben Solo actor relived some of the darker parts of his past with the massive sci-fi franchise during a recent conversation with AP.
body: "For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a Star Wars film," Driver said. "What are we debating? It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written."

We first learned about The Hunt for Ben Solo, a Skywalker Saga follow-up that explored a potential future for its title character, when Driver called it one of the "coolest scripts" he had "ever been a part of" late last year. Despite the hype, it never came to be, mostly because, according to Driver, then-Disney CEO Bob Iger and co-chairman Alan Bergman "didn't see how Ben Solo was alive."

What followed was months of additional words from those who worked on the shuttered project, including Soderbergh, who called Disney's decision to pull the plug after two-and-a-half years of work "insane." Before long, fans orchestrated their own campaign to try and save the movie, but at least as far as August 2026, Lucasfilm president Dave Filoni has said that it's not something the company is working on right now.

articles.title: Stephen King’s Underrated 1980 Horror Thriller Gets New Prime Video Adaptation
articles.summary: Stephen King fans are eating well, with Mike Flanagan's adaptation of Carrie turning out to be a surprise hit, a second season of It: Welcome to Derry on the way, and a series based on The Dark Tower books in the works. But that's not all King fans can look forward to.
body: Prime Video is reportedly developing a limited series based on King's horror-sci-fi short story Crouch End. Considered an homage to H.P. Lovecraft, the story first appeared in the New Tales of the Cthulhu Mythos anthology, and was later published in King’s Nightmares & Dreamscapes short story collection. It bears the distinction of not being set in King's native Maine, like many of his works, but rather in London.

The six-part adaptation is created by Paul Tomalin ( Bodies ) and directed by Tom Shankland ( Berlin Noir ). Variety confirms its producers include Mammoth Screen ( The Serpent ), and Fifth Season ( Severance ), while its executive producers are Paul Tomalin, Ben Irving, Rebecca Keane, Damien Timmer, and Tom Shankland.

articles.title: WoW: Forever dungeon mobs no longer give EXP if they're trivial for anyone in the party
articles.summary: It's been something of a rollercoaster watching Blizzard tweak the experience rewards players can expect from dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever. They've always been a reliable way to get oodles of experience and fat loots, but in Forever, the goal has seemingly been to ensure they're more of a…
body: Initially, mob experience values were nerfed pretty hard to compensate for a boost in quest experience, meaning that you'd get diminishing returns for spamming one dungeon over and over. Later, dungeon enemy experience was buffed by a lot, but not back to its pre-nerf value.

In a hotfix released yesterday, dungeon experience was tweaked yet again: "Killing enemies in dungeons now awards zero experience to all party members if the level of the enemy is trivial to the level of one or more of the party members," the note reads.

A mob is considered trivial in World of Warcraft when it's a significantly lower level than you (the exact threshold changes based on your level)—you'll know an enemy is trivial to your character when its level is displayed in a gray font.

This change seems aimed at higher-level players boosting their friends or a group of paying customers through instances, potentially offsetting the experience nerfs by clearing the dungeon and its quests much faster.

articles.title: Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World
articles.summary: If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin. Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together.
body: First up, I just have to gush over the artstyle a bit. The whole game is hand-drawn with a colourful, comic book look that has an impressive sense of depth to it. It gives off a deep love of Italian architecture and landscapes, and that admiration clearly extends to the food too. Once you've gotten the ingredients you need, you then, loosely in the vein of Cooking Mama, prepare them and make various classic Italian dishes by performing some quick minigames. Simple, but charming! The rest of the time you're off killing some ghoulies that look like mutated fruit and veggies, with the occasional fungus-possessed hog and, uh, haunted statues? I think?

I'm also quite pleased about two points made on the game's Steam page. First is the content description: "This game features cartoon violence, sensitive political themes set in a fictional world, and depictions of an oppressive government committing crimes against its citizens." There is clearly a romantic quality to the game and I'd be worried if it didn't acknowledge any of the political context of the decades preceding.
points: If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin.
Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed together.

articles.title: Is the game funny, or just the players? Jackbox CEO says they get 'a lot of false positives' with a staff of comedy writers
articles.summary: Social improv games like those in Jackbox 's Party Packs can have vastly different vibes depending on who you're playing with. Meemaw isn't likely to appreciate the phrase "glup shitto" the way your PC gaming friends will, and those sorts of high-variance dynamics are something Jackbox Games has to…
body: "I mean we do a ton [of testing] internally, but then as games get greenlit, we'll bring in external groups," Bilder told PC Gamer associate editor Ted Litchfield in a recent interview. "We want to make sure that we're not just local-biased with our own opinions on things. We want to make sure these games are playing well."

Something that makes it especially hard to tell whether a game is funny or they're just having a good session is the fact that they work with comedy writers—people who can make a boring game seem funny just by cracking jokes while they play.

"We get a lot of false positives because we have such funny people here that work in the office, and they make games shine," said Bilder. "No matter what the concept is, you're gonna laugh, or the way they're hosting or emceeing the game, the pitch is hilarious, and it's like, can the game do that? Or is it just [studio creative director Arnie Niekamp]? Arnie's funny … a lot of times it is just Arnie."

In the same interview, Bilder also commented on generative AI. "The people are what make this product," he said. "The comedy, the writing, and the art, all that is done by people, and we have no intention of changing that."
points: Social improv games like those in Jackbox 's Party Packs can have vastly different vibes depending on who you're playing with.

articles.title: Do you like mob tagging in oldschool MMOs, or are you done with fighting for quest credit?
articles.summary: Terminally Online. This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about…
body: I've been having a pleasant time with WoW: Forever (and by that, I mean it has consumed nearly every waking moment of my life). One thing, however, has been made pretty clear: Mob tagging, that is, only giving kill credit to the first player (or group) to damage a mob, is divisive.

One side of the fence—my side, I'm afraid—does see mob tagging as a necessary evil in an MMO that's trying to drive social interaction. Videogames, particularly ones that are incentivising you to group up, are kind of meant to be a pain in the butt sometimes; if you've got a "kill 20" quest and there another person there, the fact you might get in each other's way if you don't group up, and have a jollier time if you do, is a net good.

I have more complicated thoughts on item drop quests being bad in a group, sure. And I'd like it if Blizzard's layering technology was a little more merciful. But, overall, I'm all for it. Nearly every single person I've thrown an invite to has grouped up with me, and I've even (gasp) had conversations with strangers. Pleasant ones!

articles.title: Call of Duty Endowment marks Remembrance Day with veterans' Valor Pack push
articles.summary: The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.
body: The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.
The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.
According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.
To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

body: Friend Request is an early storyline mission in Grand Theft Auto 5. Tutorials are behind us, but Trevor hasn't joined the team yet. Retired crook Michael De Santa is in deep trouble, so he turns to his old accomplice Lester for help. The software enthusiast seems willing to set up a new job, but first he needs Michael to blow open the walled garden that is Jay Norris’s skull.
GTA’s legendary, long campaigns demand frequent changes of pace, and cooldown character studies like Friend Request offer a different kind of exploration than open-world adventure.

Trekking through trauma, wandering through wounded pride, we’re given space to dig beneath the skin of the people we embody and understand what drives them. This is the art of the level for Grand Theft Auto 5.

videos.title: Crimson Desert: Charting the Unknown Review
videos.summary: Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown DLC reviewed by Travis Northup on PC and Xbox Series X, also available on PlayStation 5.
body: "Crimson Desert’s Charting the Unknown DLC is unlikely to win over anyone who hadn’t already fallen in love with this massive world, but it does successfully expand a game that already had a staggering amount of stuff to do. Diving around underwater ruins and exploring islands for treasure is a good time, even if the ship exploration and combat on the way to that seafaring content is a bore. Elsewhere, some of the new activities like a business management minigame and NPC dating are absolutely worth adding to your backlog of quests to tackle. Those side distractions continue to be the true appeal of Crimson Desert, but it’s a shame that the new story questlines that act as an extended epilogue are largely as dull as they are inaccessible. Overall, Charting the Unknown is just more Crimson Desert, with its “jack of all trades, master of none” philosophy fully intact. If you’re hundreds of hours deep and that’s all you want, it will almost certainly deliver – but if you’re not, it’s not the most convincing reason to come back."

Overall, Charting the Unknown is just more Crimson Desert, with its “jack of all trades, master of none” philosophy fully intact.
